If you're like the majority of e-commerce brands then you're probably feeling the pinch right now.

Ad costs are rising by the day as the gods at Facebook and Google continue to monopolize the market.

Jeff and his crew over at Amazon are squeezing you even tighter leaving your margins a mere shadow of what they used to be.

Influencer marketing has become saturated and all the best influencers have been picked up by the bigger brands with the deepest pockets or even worse, they've started their own brands in competition with you.

The list just goes on and on...

It's hard not to feel like the odds are stacked against you.

But what if I was to tell you that there is a solution.

A proven system that you can use to 2X your sales conversions and increase your margins so you can actually breathe...

A system that has been battle-tested and iterated upon 1000 times over the course of 25 years with some of the fastest-growing e-commerce brands on the planet.

A system that has taken brands from relative obscurity to 8-figure household names.

A system that has taken brands from tens of millions of dollars in debt (ouch) and turned them into hyper-profitable cash generating machines that have investors fighting over them.

A system that stacks all of the chips on your side.

A system that doesn't involve hoping, praying, or sheer luck.

Not the latest tactic, hack, or strategy that works today but is dead by lunchtime tomorrow...

A methodology that allows you to thrive regardless of what is going on in the economy (in fact, historically speaking, it has performed even BETTER during downturns).

A holistic methodology that is the result of more than 25 years in the trenches working with e-commerce brands and consulting with some of the biggest names in the E-Commerce marketing space such as Gary Vee, Neil Patel, and Matt Higgins.

A secret weapon that up until now has only been accessible to a select few who have used it again, and again, and again to experience explosive growth with predictability.

My name is Sabir Semerkant and I call this methodology "The 8D Method"...

...and if you are an e-commerce business that is struggling to hit your targets and looking for rapid growth then this is the answer to your prayers.

You see most E-Commerce businesses fail NOT because they don't have a great product, service, story, or brand, but because they get too busy running the business and never get the chance to sit down and optimize all 8 key pillars of the business, or as I like to call them, Dimensions, and end up running a suboptimal business that robs them of their profit margins and makes it impossible to scale."

But imagine what it would feel like to unlock that growth.

To be in complete control and have the ability to grow your sales with predictability while maximizing your margins regardless of what is happening in the market.

What would that mean for your brand?

Or more importantly, what would this mean for you and your entire company?

More profits.

More exposure.

More influence.

More investment.

More fun.

Probably.

But more than anything, this methodology gives you the one thing that every business owner on the planet wants...

More FREEDOM.

Freedom to grow your brand ON YOUR TERMS.

The freedom to invest in long-term strategies that will yield even bigger returns down the road.

The freedom to think big and stop worrying about just getting by.

The freedom to thrive.

No more hoping and praying that your marketing dollars produce a ROAS above breakeven.

No more relying on Uncle Facebook and Aunt Google to bring home the bacon so you can pay your staff.

No more feeling like you are rolling the dice every single month and crossing your fingers that this isn't the month when the wheels fall off and it all goes horribly wrong.

Just complete clarity and confidence that your brand is on the right track with the right strategies in place to grow PROFITABLY.

Here are just a few of my success stories to date using this method:

✅ Ashley Stewart from 3M - 30M in under 2 years

✅ The Vitamin Shoppe from 12M - 55M in 4.5 years

✅ Carol's Daughter from 3M - 10M in 2 years

🔥 In fact, in 2024 alone I helped 29 E-Commerce brands across 17 different product categories (and spanning 13 different countries) grow by an average of 108% in under 21 days by implementing on the first of the 8 dimensions.

👉 Brands like The Aurum Brothers, a Netherlands based mens jewelry brand, who were stuck at 1.5M for more than 2 years and felt like they had tried everything and experienced a 146% increase in sales in 3 weeks.

👉 Brands like global luxury luggage company Globe Trotter who experienced a 333% increase in conversions across all 3 of their international stores.

👉 Brands like women’s water-sports and professional swimwear business Wallien, who saw an 88% increase in sales in under 30 days.

And now I've made this exact framework public for the very first time.

CLICK BELOW NOW to learn more...

https://growthbysabir.com/rapid2x/

HERE'S WHAT YOU'LL LEARN:

✅ Why the "1.7-second rule" needs to be at the core of all of your marketing campaigns and how to use this insight to hack consumer psychology and make your ads and store convert like crazy.

✅ Why “conversion rate” is actually a terrible KPI and the one key metric you should track instead.

✅ Why regular discounting is actually hurting your conversions and how to optimize your pricing strategy to increase conversions while INCREASING your margins and ROAS.

Go see for yourself:

https://growthbysabir.com/rapid2x/

I was holding her hand when it happened.

We were eating lunch. She was telling me about her garden — the tomatoes weren’t doing well this year, too much rain — and mid-sentence, her face changed.

Her left side just… stopped.

The fork clattered to the floor. Her mouth drooped. She tried to speak and nothing came out but a moan that didn’t sound human.

I called 911. Rode in the ambulance. Watched them wheel her into the ER.

She was 64 years old. She’d been on blood pressure medication for twelve years. Three different pills. Lisinopril. Amlodipine. Hydrochlorothiazide.

She took them every single day. Never missed a dose.

The stroke took her anyway.

For the next two years, my mother couldn’t speak. Couldn’t say my name. Couldn’t tell her grandchildren she loved them. She’d look at us with eyes that still had everything behind them — the frustration, the fear, the things she desperately wanted to say — but nothing came out.

She died at 66, trapped inside a body that had betrayed her.

I was already a grown woman when she passed. I swore I would never end up like her.

Five years later, I was sitting in my cardiologist’s office when he frowned at my blood pressure reading.

152/92.

“Sarah, this is stroke territory. We need to start medication immediately.”

My hands went cold. Not from poor circulation. From the memory of my mother’s face going slack over a plate of pasta.

“What medication?” I asked, already knowing.

“Lisinopril to start. We’ll add others if needed.”

Lisinopril. The same pill my mother took every morning for twelve years before her brain exploded.

“No.”

He looked up from his prescription pad.

“Excuse me?”

“I watched my mother take those pills for twelve years. She never missed a dose. She still had the stroke. She still lost her voice. She still died without being able to say goodbye to her grandchildren.”

I was crying. I couldn’t stop.

“I need to try something else first. Anything else.”

He sighed. “Sarah, I understand the trauma. But the medication—”

“Didn’t save her. It didn’t save her.”

He paused. Set down his pen.

“I can give you 60 days. But if you’re not below 130/80, we start medication. Non-negotiable. Your mother’s stroke makes you high-risk. I won’t watch you follow the same path.”

60 days. To figure out what went wrong with my mother. And make sure it didn’t happen to me.

That night, I couldn’t sleep.

I kept seeing her face. The fork falling. The moan.

At 2 AM, I was at my computer, searching: “why blood pressure medication doesn’t prevent stroke,” “high blood pressure natural alternatives,” “what actually lowers blood pressure.”

I wasn’t just looking for solutions. I was looking for answers.

Why didn’t the medication save her? She did everything right. Three pills. Every day. For twelve years. And it still wasn’t enough.

I needed to understand why. Because if I was going to end up in the same place, I at least wanted to know why I was dying.

Three weeks into my search, I found something that changed everything.

Not a cure. An explanation.

Blood pressure medication doesn’t fix the underlying problem. It forces your blood vessels to relax artificially. The moment you stop taking it, your pressure rebounds — often higher than before.

That’s why doctors say “you’ll be on this forever.” It’s not treatment. It’s management. Your body becomes dependent on the drug to do what it should be doing naturally.

My mother’s body forgot how to regulate itself. After twelve years on medication, her cardiovascular system was completely dependent on pills that were masking the problem, not solving it.

The stroke wasn’t despite the medication.

It was almost inevitable because of it.

One thing kept appearing in legitimate research: dietary nitrates.

Not the nitrates in processed meat. Dietary nitrates from vegetables — especially beetroot.

Nitrate content: Not listed.

I was holding her hand when it happened.

We were eating lunch. She was telling me about her garden — the tomatoes weren’t doing well this year, too much rain — and mid-sentence, her face changed.

Her left side just… stopped.

The fork clattered to the floor. Her mouth drooped. She tried to speak and nothing came out but a moan that didn’t sound human.

I called 911. Rode in the ambulance. Watched them wheel her into the ER.

She was 64 years old. She’d been on blood pressure medication for twelve years. Three different pills. Lisinopril. Amlodipine. Hydrochlorothiazide.

She took them every single day. Never missed a dose.

The stroke took her anyway.

For the next two years, my mother couldn’t speak. Couldn’t say my name. Couldn’t tell her grandchildren she loved them. She’d look at us with eyes that still had everything behind them — the frustration, the fear, the things she desperately wanted to say — but nothing came out.

She died at 66, trapped inside a body that had betrayed her.

I was already a grown woman when she passed. I swore I would never end up like her.

Five years later, I was sitting in my cardiologist’s office when he frowned at my blood pressure reading.

152/92.

“Sarah, this is stroke territory. We need to start medication immediately.”

My hands went cold. Not from poor circulation. From the memory of my mother’s face going slack over a plate of pasta.

“What medication?” I asked, already knowing.

“Lisinopril to start. We’ll add others if needed.”

Lisinopril. The same pill my mother took every morning for twelve years before her brain exploded.

“No.”

He looked up from his prescription pad.

“Excuse me?”

“I watched my mother take those pills for twelve years. She never missed a dose. She still had the stroke. She still lost her voice. She still died without being able to say goodbye to her grandchildren.”

I was crying. I couldn’t stop.

“I need to try something else first. Anything else.”

He sighed. “Sarah, I understand the trauma. But the medication—”

“Didn’t save her. It didn’t save her.”

He paused. Set down his pen.

“I can give you 60 days. But if you’re not below 130/80, we start medication. Non-negotiable. Your mother’s stroke makes you high-risk. I won’t watch you follow the same path.”

60 days. To figure out what went wrong with my mother. And make sure it didn’t happen to me.

That night, I couldn’t sleep.

I kept seeing her face. The fork falling. The moan.

At 2 AM, I was at my computer, searching: “why blood pressure medication doesn’t prevent stroke,” “high blood pressure natural alternatives,” “what actually lowers blood pressure.”

I wasn’t just looking for solutions. I was looking for answers.

Why didn’t the medication save her? She did everything right. Three pills. Every day. For twelve years. And it still wasn’t enough.

I needed to understand why. Because if I was going to end up in the same place, I at least wanted to know why I was dying.

Not a cure. An explanation.

Blood pressure medication doesn’t fix the underlying problem. It forces your blood vessels to relax artificially. The moment you stop taking it, your pressure rebounds — often higher than before.

My mother’s body forgot how to regulate itself. After twelve years on medication, her cardiovascular system was completely dependent on pills that were masking the problem, not solving it.

The stroke wasn’t despite the medication.

It was almost inevitable because of it.

Nitrate content: Not listed.

Organic beet juice from Whole Foods. Same.

I wasn’t. That was the point.

I found a study that made me sick to my stomach.

Researchers tested 47 commercial beetroot supplements for actual nitrate content.

The variance was FIFTY TIMES.

Some had 5mg per serving. Some had 250mg. Most had less than 50mg. All labeled simply as “beetroot powder.”

To get 400mg of nitrates from most brands, you’d need to take 8–10 capsules per serving. Minimum. And even then, you’re guessing.

Most supplement companies use heat processing to make beetroot powder. It’s faster. It’s cheaper. It destroys up to 90% of the nitrates.

“124 over 76.”

“That’s a 28-point drop,” I said. “In 60 days.”
